name: MicroC p53
description:
MicroC with a switchable p53 mutation, driven from the Planner. Keeps microc.json and every function it uses untouched so the two can be compared. Three differences:
(1) gene_update uses propagate_gene_networks_single_gene -- the NetLogo single-gene random update from opencellcomms_engine/benchmarks/gene_network_standalone.py -- instead of the graph walk. Fate nodes are ordinary nodes here, read directly rather than latched as transient triggers, which is what makes results comparable with that benchmark.
(2) fix_gene_nodes clamps genes for the whole run, heritably across division. p53 has a logic rule, so without a clamp it is recomputed every step and reactivates from growth-factor signalling. With p53 held OFF, Apoptosis = !BCL2 & !ERK & FOXO3 & p53 is unsatisfiable, so the tumour proliferates; with it ON, apoptosis and growth arrest dominate. Both the knockout table and the propagation step count are wired parameter nodes, so they appear in the Planner.
(3) a fate_summary behavior records the per-iteration fate, phenotype and population census, tracking p53 and p38 so the clamp can be seen holding.
propagation_steps is 1000, not microc.json's 5: one gene moves per step and jaya.bnd has 81 updatable genes, so Proliferation -- behind an 11-layer glycolysis chain -- needs ~1000 steps to become reachable at all, while Apoptosis is ~6 layers deep.

__world__.description: MicroC: __world__ (sets up the world: simulation, domain, the empty population container bound to the domain grid, substances, associations)

functions.description: Initialize simulation infrastructure
Define 2D spatial domain
Create the (empty) cell population container bound to the domain grid. Cells are placed later by the agent init (read_checkpoint).
Configure all substance-to-gene associations
Metabolism model constants (Michaelis-Menten laws used by the coupled diffusion solver). Equations documented in the node source.

tumor_cell_create.description: MicroC: tumor_cell_create (seeds the tumor_cell agents into the world: load cells from checkpoint, then build per-cell gene networks)

functions.description: Read checkpoint file with cell positions and gene states. If gene states are present, initializes them.
Initialize NetLogo-faithful gene networks for all cells
Clamp genes for the whole run (heritable across division). p53 OFF = tumour.
Wrap the loaded cells in an abm_population so MicroC runs on the ABM motor

diffusion_step.description: MicroC coupled diffusion (SPECIAL CASE): one Picard-coupled PDE solves ALL substance fields (Oxygen, Glucose, Lactate, H, TGFA, FGF, HGF, GI) together, so no single substance owns it -- deliberately homed as a World behavior, not per-resource, which is why the resource_kinds intentionally carry empty behaviors.

functions.description: MicroC metabolic model — per-cell O2/glucose consumption and lactate/proton production. The solver calls this once per coupling iteration.
COUPLED solver - iterative coupling with under-relaxation. Physically correct, prevents negative concentrations.
Generate iteration-specific plots (Oxygen, Glucose, Lactate) using AutoPlotter
Translate substance concentrations → gene input states via associations
NetLogo single-gene random update (matches gene_network_standalone.py); honours gene clamps
Mark cells as necrotic based on user-defined conditions
Track cells in Growth_Arrest state with time limit
Mark cells as apoptotic based on gene network Apoptosis output
Mark cells as Proliferation or Quiescence based on gene network
Handle cell division for proliferating cells
Remove cells with Apoptosis phenotype from population
Generate final state visualization

symbiosis_summary.description: MicroC: symbiosis_summary (per-iteration CSV for the metabolic-symbiosis figures -- cells by ATP pathway, cells by oxygen region, and the metabolic symbiosis index)

functions.description: One CSV row per iteration: cells by ATP pathway (glycoATP / mitoATP / total), cells by oxygen region (oxygenated / hypoxic), and the metabolic symbiosis index. MSI is emitted twice because 'lactate metabolic' has two defensible readings in jaya.bnd: msi_mct1 counts only cells importing lactate (MCT1 ON), msi_mito counts any oxidative cell (mitoATP ON, which includes glucose-fed ones).

subworkflow_calls.description: symbiosis_summary (placed before division, so the census matches the fates just marked). Must NOT carry for_each: record_metabolic_symbiosis is a whole-population reporter that writes one row per iteration.

fate_summary (before division, so marked phenotypes are still visible). Must NOT carry for_each. With kind: tumor_cell it does not run at all -- MicroC deliberately leaves metabolic_state['_kind'] untagged (see build_tumor_cell_abm_population), so agents_of_kind('tumor_cell') is empty and the log reads "Running 'fate_summary' over 0 tumor_cell(s)". A kind-less per-agent ask is no better: record_gene_fate_counts is a whole-population reporter with no env.cell guard, so it would write one duplicate census row per cell and zero out the fires/reverts deltas.
